messages.content:
You are a clinical reasoning assistant for emergency physicians (vertigo). You explain, in clear clinical English, the result of a deterministic decision-support engine. The engine decides; you only explain. The physician decides.

Input (JSON): `confirmed_values` (findings confirmed by the physician), `result` (the engine's urgency, red flags, differential diagnosis, forced and blocked actions) and `grounding` (clinical criteria fragments, each with a `chunk_id` and `text`; they may be in Spanish).

Mandatory rules:
- `explanation`: 3 to 6 sentences explaining why the engine reached that urgency and that differential, from the confirmed findings and the fragments provided. Do not invent findings.
- `reconciliation`: one or two sentences explaining how findings pointing to a peripheral cause are reconciled with those pointing to a central cause, if any. Remember that urgency is set by the deterministic engine.
- `suggested_next_steps`: up to 4 short evaluation steps (no treatments or doses), consistent with the forced actions and never proposing a blocked action.
- `suggested_urgency`: null unless the engine's result seems inconsistent with the findings to you; it never replaces the engine's urgency.
- `cited_chunk_ids`: only `chunk_id`s present in `grounding` that you actually used. Never cite identifiers you were not given.
- Tone: decision support, not a definitive diagnosis. No identifying data.
- Write every text field in English.

{"confirmed_values":{"age_years":45,"dix_hallpike":"right_positive","duration":"seconds","focal_signs.diplopia":false,"focal_signs.dysarthria":false,"hearing_loss":"none","nystagmus_fatigable":true,"timing_pattern":"episodic_triggered","tinnitus":false,"torsion_confirmed_by_clinician":true,"trigger":"positional_head"},"grounding":[{"chunk_id":"clinibrium-paraphrase:bppv_posterior-1","text":"El VPPB de canal posterior se presenta como vértigo breve (típicamente menos de un minuto) desencadenado por cambios de posición de la cabeza — girarse en la cama, mirar hacia arriba, agacharse — con nistagmo torsional-vertical que aparece tras una latencia corta y se fatiga con la repetición de la maniobra. Es la causa más frecuente de vértigo periférico y la más tratable en sitio, mediante la maniobra de Epley."},{"chunk_id":"clinibrium-paraphrase:bppv_posterior-2","text":"El signo de cabecera confirmatorio es la maniobra de Dix-Hallpike positiva del lado sintomático, con nistagmo upbeating y componente torsional hacia el oído afectado. La confirmación clínica de la componente torsional es el gold-standard para distinguir el canal posterior del horizontal. El cuadro no asocia hipoacusia ni síntomas neurovegetativos marcados."},{"chunk_id":"clinibrium-paraphrase:bppv_posterior-3","text":"Manejo: maniobra de Epley en la consulta como primera línea, con tasas de resolución del 60-80% en una sola sesión. La maniobra de Semont es una alternativa. Si fracasan, se consideran los programas domiciliario de Brandt-Daroff. No requiere imagen ni estudio de laboratorio en el cuadro típico."},{"chunk_id":"clinibrium-paraphrase:bppv_horizontal-1","text":"El VPPB de canal horizontal se sospecha cuando el vértigo posicional se acompaña de nistagmo horizontal puro desencadenado por la prueba de supine roll (Pagnini-McClure). A diferencia del canal posterior, el nistagmo puede no fatigarse tan rápidamente y puede cambiar de dirección según el lado evaluado."}],"lang":"en","result":{"blocked_actions":[],"differential":[{"diagnosis":"bppv_posterior","score_pct":92},{"diagnosis":"bppv_horizontal","score_pct":69},{"diagnosis":"vestibular_migraine","score_pct":27},{"diagnosis":"vestibular_neuritis","score_pct":10}],"forced_actions":[],"red_flags":[],"urgency":"ambulatoria"}}

response.content: {"cited_chunk_ids": ["clinibrium-paraphrase:bppv_posterior-1", "clinibrium-paraphrase:bppv_posterior-2", "clinibrium-paraphrase:bppv_horizontal-1", "clinibrium-paraphrase:bppv_posterior-3"], "explanation": "The engine assigned ambulatoria urgency with posterior canal BPPV as the leading diagnosis because the vertigo lasts seconds with a positional head trigger in an episodic-triggered pattern. The right-positive Dix-Hallpike with clinician-confirmed torsion and fatigable nystagmus matches the confirmatory bedside pattern for posterior canal involvement. Absence of hearing loss and tinnitus further supports a typical posterior canal picture without cochlear involvement. Horizontal canal BPPV scored lower because no pure horizontal nystagmus on supine roll was confirmed and confirmed torsion favors posterior over horizontal canal. No red flags, diplopia, or dysarthria were confirmed, supporting ambulatory management without imaging in the typical presentation.", "reconciliation": "All confirmed findings point toward a peripheral positional cause with no conflicting central features to reconcile. The absence of diplopia and dysarthria argues against a central mimic in this presentation.", "suggested_next_steps": ["Repeat Dix-Hallpike documenting latency, direction, torsion and fatigability", "Perform supine roll test to assess for horizontal canal nystagmus", "Complete focused neurologic and oculomotor examination", "Review positional triggers and associated auditory symptoms"], "suggested_urgency": null}
